role.altitude: The controller stops preparing the close, the audit file and the tax pack by hand. Instead they design the system that prepares them. They own the accrual handbook, the tie-out queries, the materiality thresholds, the mandate matrix and the audit trail. Models draft and deterministic checks decide. The controller approves, handles exceptions and improves the rules after each close.
reach: FP&A Analyst: monthly variance and flux commentary per site and per customer
Accountant: first draft of accruals, reclasses and the fixed asset roll-forward
Bookkeeper: review of AFAS bank matching exceptions and duplicate invoice checks
Payroll Specialist: reconciling payroll journals to the general ledger, and the loonheffing tie-out
Finance Director: options memos on lease-or-buy and investment deductions for the board
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: cost of flex labour per site from agency invoices joined to AFAS hours
role.ceiling_note: Out of roughly 1,600 hours a year, these seven tasks take about 280. About 110 of those can be freed. The ceiling is set by judgement and accountability, not by drafting speed. Estimates, tax positions, the auditor relationship and signing rights stay with a person. Benchmarks are US GAAP, and Dutch GAAP (BW 2 Titel 9), Vpb and VAT are untested. Nothing posts or files without a tie-out and a named approver.
skills_to_grow: Writing accrual and control rules precise enough for a model and a check to follow
SQL or Power Query on the AFAS extract, to build tie-out and exception queries
Prompt and evaluation design: test sets of past closes to measure draft quality
AI governance in finance: logging, auditor-reproducible evidence, the EU AI Act and AVG for any personal data
Scenario modelling and explaining options to non-finance managers
role.ambitious_version: Close in three working days with a rolling 13-week cash forecast and a site-level forecast the business trusts. The audit file builds itself all year from logged tie-outs. Every site manager gets a monthly one-page cost explanation they can question in Teams. The controller spends the freed time on margin per customer contract and on flex labour economics.

tasks.short: Answer budget holders and site managers on budget rules, cost codes and spending policy.

today.trigger: A question by mail or Teams from a site manager, HR or purchasing, or a new budget round
steps: Read the question and find the relevant policy on SharePoint
Check the budget position in Power BI or AFAS
Write an answer or explain it in a call
Repeat the same explanation to other sites
drudgery: The same cost-code and capex-versus-opex questions from three sites
Looking up which version of the policy applies
today.time_sinks: Repeated questions and searching for the current policy text.

lenses.faster: A Teams assistant answers from the SharePoint finance handbook and the budget position, with a link to the source. The controller sees only the questions it cannot answer.
lenses.autonomous: When a budget holder goes over 90% of budget, they get a note explaining the rule and the next step.
lenses.ambitious: Every site manager gets a monthly page in plain Dutch on their own cost lines, for the first time.
lenses.joy: No more typing the same explanation of cost codes; the conversations that remain are about real trade-offs.
lenses.options: For a spending question, the assistant sets out two or three compliant routes (budget shift, capex request, defer).
lenses.altitude: The controller maintains the handbook and the answer set and reviews unanswered questions monthly.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a rule should bend, and holding a site manager to a budget face to face.
tasks.pattern_why: The answers shape how people spend money and sometimes need judgement. The controller stays the lead, and the model handles the standard answers from the handbook.

in_practice.trigger: A question in the Finance Teams channel, or a budget threshold crossed in the nightly Power BI refresh
steps: The assistant retrieves the policy text from SharePoint and the budget line from the AFAS extract
It drafts an answer that cites the source
Standard answers go out; anything outside the handbook goes to the controller
The controller answers and adds the case to the handbook
in_practice.human_gate: Any answer that grants an exception or commits budget
data_needed: Budget versus actual per cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint Q&A log in the finance site

evidence.claim: Retrieval-based assistants over policy documents in SharePoint and Teams can answer routine questions with source links
Leaving client communication and tacit context to people fits what lab tests did not measure

risks: Answers based on an outdated policy version
Budget holders treat the assistant's answer as approval
research_questions: What share of the controller's mail and Teams questions over three months are repeats covered by the handbook?
Is the SharePoint finance handbook current enough to serve as the single source?
Do site managers use a Teams assistant, or do they keep calling?

tasks.short: Dig into site, customer and cost figures to find where margin leaks and what to improve.

today.trigger: Month close, the forecast cycle or a question from the Finance Director
steps: Export from Power BI and AFAS to Excel
Build pivots by site, customer and cost type
Compare with budget, last year and agency invoices
Write findings for the MT pack
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel pivots every month
Matching agency invoices to hours by hand
today.time_sinks: Data preparation and reconciling sources, before any analysis can start.

lenses.faster: After the nightly refresh, a model drafts flux commentary and a ranked list of variances by site. The controller checks the top items instead of building pivots.
lenses.autonomous: Each month after close, an exception list runs: flex cost per hour against the agency contract rate, and margin per customer below threshold.
lenses.ambitious: Margin per customer contract and per warehouse zone every month, which nobody has had the time to build.
lenses.joy: No pivot rebuilding; the time goes on asking why Venlo's overtime rose.
lenses.options: For each finding, two or three improvement options with an estimated effect for the MT.
lenses.altitude: The controller defines the variance thresholds and drivers, and audits the commentary for errors.
reach: People Analytics flex labour cost analysis

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which numbers reflect operational reality and which are posting artefacts, and choosing what is worth raising with the MT.
tasks.pattern_why: Finding improvements needs business judgement. The model speeds up preparation and drafting, while the controller picks and frames the findings.

in_practice.trigger: Month-close status set to 'ledger closed' in AFAS
steps: Deterministic queries compute variances on the Power BI dataset
A model drafts commentary and candidate causes per variance above threshold
The controller verifies causes with site managers and selects findings
Approved findings go into the MT pack
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves every finding before it reaches the MT
data_needed: Ledger by cost centre and customer
in_practice.logs_to: Monthly analysis folder on SharePoint with drafts and approved versions

evidence.claim: The leading model met 61.8% of criteria on 160 close tasks; the bottleneck is accounting judgement
Accountants using AI closed the month 7.5 days faster across 79 firms
evidence.source: Choi and Xie via CFO Dive [S8]

evidence.claim: Products draft flux commentary for people to approve

risks: A plausible but wrong explanation of a variance reaches the MT
Operational volume data is not in the AFAS extract
research_questions: Can pallets and order volumes per site be joined to the AFAS extract in Power BI?
How many draft explanations does the controller accept unchanged across three closes?
Do agency invoice lines carry enough detail to match hours per site?

tasks.short: Run the year-end audit with the external accountant and check our own controls during the year.

today.trigger: Interim and year-end audit planning by the external auditor, or a control issue
steps: Receive the PBC list from the auditor
Collect ledger extracts, contracts and reconciliations from AFAS and SharePoint
Answer auditor queries and sample requests
Follow up on management letter points
drudgery: Reformatting AFAS exports for the auditor
today.time_sinks: Collecting evidence for samples and answering follow-up questions.

lenses.faster: An agent works through the PBC list, pulls extracts and documents and maps each to its item. The controller reviews the file before it goes out.
lenses.autonomous: Every month, deterministic tests run on journals (postings after close, round amounts, the same user creating and approving, bank detail changes) and the exceptions are logged.
lenses.ambitious: Controls are tested all year, so the audit becomes a review of logged evidence, with fewer audit adjustments.
lenses.joy: No chasing PDFs for samples; the time goes on the discussions with the auditor that matter.
lenses.options: For each management letter point, a few remediation designs with their cost.
lenses.altitude: The controller designs the control tests and the evidence file and decides what is material.

tasks.human_edge: The relationship with the auditor, judging what is material, and accountability for management's statements.
tasks.pattern_why: Compiling evidence takes several steps across systems and has exceptions. Nothing goes to the auditor until the controller approves it.

in_practice.trigger: The PBC list is received, or the monthly close is completed
steps: Run journal entry tests and reconciliations as fixed queries
The agent collects documents per PBC item from AFAS and SharePoint
The agent flags missing or inconsistent items
The controller reviews and releases the package to the auditor
in_practice.human_gate: The controller signs off each package before it is sent
data_needed: Ledger and journal logs with user IDs
in_practice.logs_to: Audit evidence library on SharePoint with a run log per test

evidence.claim: Estimates the auditor cannot rebuild, because prompts and outputs sit in personal accounts, are a known risk
Products keep agent output for audit ('Retain for Audit')

risks: The auditor does not accept AI-compiled evidence without proof of how it was produced
An agent shares documents containing personal data (salaries) beyond what was requested, an AVG issue
research_questions: Will our external auditor rely on logged automated journal tests?
Which AFAS log tables show who created and approved each journal?
How many hours went into PBC collection last year?

tasks.short: Write and update finance controls: procuratieregeling, payment approvals, credit limits, budget rules.

today.trigger: An audit finding, a new system or process, or the yearly policy review
steps: Review the existing policy and audit points
Draft changes in Word
Align with the Finance Director and the department heads
Publish on SharePoint and set up approvals in AFAS
drudgery: Keeping policy text and AFAS workflow settings consistent
today.time_sinks: Drafting and redrafting, and checking that AFAS workflows match the written policy.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the policy change from audit findings and the current text, and lists the AFAS workflow settings that must change.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly check compares the mandate matrix with actual approvers in AFAS and reports mismatches.
lenses.ambitious: Proper written controls for flex worker invoices and agency orders, which are mostly informal today.
lenses.joy: No formatting or version chasing; the controller decides on control design.
lenses.options: Two or three control designs per risk (preventive, detective, threshold variants) with workload estimates.
lenses.altitude: The controller keeps the mandate matrix as a structured record that drives both the policy text and the AFAS workflows.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing how much control the company can carry, and getting department heads to accept it.
tasks.pattern_why: Drafting can be automated, but the trade-off between risk and workload is the controller's call, and the result binds others.

in_practice.trigger: An audit management letter point or the annual review date
steps: The model drafts changes from the finding, current policy and peer practice
The controller selects a design and edits it
The mandate matrix is updated as a structured table
Deterministic checks compare the AFAS workflow settings with the matrix
in_practice.human_gate: The Finance Director approves the policy, and the controller approves the workflow changes
in_practice.logs_to: Policy register on SharePoint with version history

evidence.claim: Mandates and signing rights work well as deterministic records
Models draft structured policy text from existing documents well

risks: Generic control text that does not fit how Noordhaven actually works
Expense or monitoring rules that touch employee data may need works council (OR) consent under WOR art. 27
research_questions: Can AFAS workflow approval settings be exported to compare with a mandate matrix?
Which current finance policies would need OR consent if changed?
How many audit points last year came from policy and workflow mismatch?

tasks.short: Prepare the Vpb pack and VAT reconciliations so our tax adviser can file the returns.

today.trigger: Year-end for Vpb; monthly or quarterly VAT deadlines
steps: Pull trial balance and VAT accounts from AFAS
Prepare the commercial-to-fiscal reconciliation in Excel
Reconcile the VAT return to the ledger
Answer adviser questions and approve filing
drudgery: Rebuilding the fiscal reconciliation workbook every year
Hunting VAT differences line by line
today.time_sinks: Reconciling VAT and collecting support for the fiscal adjustments.

lenses.faster: An agent builds the tax pack from AFAS (trial balance, fiscal adjustment candidates such as gemengde kosten and representation) and reconciles VAT to the ledger. The controller reviews the differences.
lenses.autonomous: A VAT tie-out runs at each period end and flags differences before the return is due.
lenses.ambitious: A tax position file kept current all year instead of rebuilt in a rush at year-end.
lenses.joy: No line-by-line VAT hunts; what remains is discussing positions with the adviser.
lenses.options: For uncertain items, the pack shows the treatments and their tax effect side by side.
lenses.altitude: The controller keeps the fiscal mapping rules and the tie-out queries, and reviews exceptions.

tasks.human_edge: Signing off tax positions and answering to the Belastingdienst and the adviser.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps and exceptions across AFAS and Excel. Tax estimates need mandatory human review with timestamped logs.

in_practice.trigger: Period end for VAT, and the year-end close for Vpb
steps: Deterministic VAT tie-out between return boxes and ledger
The agent drafts the commercial-to-fiscal reconciliation from mapped accounts
The agent lists items needing judgement with support
The controller reviews, adjusts and sends to the tax adviser
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves the pack, and the adviser and director approve the filing
in_practice.logs_to: Tax file on SharePoint with a timestamped run log

evidence.claim: Tax estimates need mandatory human review and approval with timestamped logs
Dutch VAT and Vpb work is untested in AI benchmarks

risks: Wrong fiscal treatment of a mixed-cost item that slips through
Reliance on a US-trained model for Dutch tax rules
research_questions: Are AFAS VAT codes clean enough for an automatic box-to-ledger tie-out?
What would the tax adviser accept as input format and support?
How many hours went into last year's Vpb pack?

tasks.short: Work out tax-smart timing of investments and structure, such as EIA and MIA for electric trucks.

today.trigger: Investment plans, the budget round or year-end
steps: List planned investments and their timing
Check schemes (KIA, EIA, MIA/Vamil) and rates
Model the tax effect in Excel
Discuss with the tax adviser and Finance Director
drudgery: Looking up scheme rules and yearly lists
today.time_sinks: Researching which schemes apply and building scenarios.

lenses.faster: A model screens the investment plan against EIA, MIA and KIA lists and drafts a scenario sheet. The adviser confirms.
lenses.autonomous: An alert when a capex request in AFAS matches a scheme with a filing deadline (EIA must be reported within three months).
lenses.ambitious: Every truck, forklift and solar panel investment screened, so no deduction is missed.
lenses.joy: No hunting through scheme lists; the work is choosing timing with the Finance Director.
lenses.options: Three to five timing and financing scenarios with their tax effect.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the screening checklist and the deadline rules.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing a tax position and taking responsibility for it with the adviser.
tasks.pattern_why: Planning is judgement with tax liability attached. The model widens the options and the controller and adviser decide.

in_practice.trigger: A capex request created, or the budget round starting
steps: The model matches the investment to scheme lists
It drafts scenarios with tax effect and deadlines
The controller reviews them and the adviser confirms
The deadline is logged in the finance calendar
in_practice.human_gate: The tax adviser and the controller approve any position

evidence.claim: Models can screen plans against published scheme lists and draft scenarios
Dutch tax is untested in accounting benchmarks

risks: An outdated scheme list or rate
Missing the three-month EIA/MIA reporting deadline if the alert fails
research_questions: How many investments in the last three years qualified for EIA or MIA but were not claimed?
Can capex requests in AFAS carry an asset type field to trigger screening?
Does the tax adviser offer this screening already, and at what cost?

tasks.short: Set depreciation terms for trucks, forklifts and racking and advise on lease versus buy.

today.trigger: A new asset purchase, a lease decision or the annual asset review
steps: Decide the useful life and residual value per asset class
Enter assets in AFAS fixed assets
Model lease versus buy in Excel
Advise the Finance Director or site manager
drudgery: Checking the asset register against invoices
today.time_sinks: Register maintenance and one-off models per decision.

lenses.faster: Asset class rules set life and residual value automatically in AFAS. A template model does lease versus buy from the quote in minutes.
lenses.autonomous: Capitalisation of invoices above the threshold is proposed automatically, and depreciation runs each month with a roll-forward tie-out.
lenses.ambitious: A fleet-wide review of replace, lease or keep for every truck and forklift each year.
lenses.joy: No register reconciling by hand; the work is advising on fleet choices.
lenses.options: Lease, buy and keep-longer scenarios with cash, P&L and tax effect side by side.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the asset class table and the capitalisation threshold.

tasks.human_edge: Judging the real useful life of equipment with operations, and advising on fleet decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: Rates, thresholds and schedules are written rules on structured data. The advisory part uses a copilot scenario template.

in_practice.trigger: A purchase invoice above the capitalisation threshold is booked, or a lease quote is received
steps: A rule proposes capitalisation and the asset class
AFAS calculates the depreciation schedule
The roll-forward tie-out checks register against ledger
The controller reviews exceptions and lease-buy scenarios
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves new asset classes, life changes and advice
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS fixed asset register and the monthly tie-out report

evidence.claim: The model drafts and the tie-out decides; nothing posts until it ties
Agents draft entries and people accept, adjust or reject them

risks: A wrong life for a new asset class distorts the P&L for years
Lease classification under Dutch GAAP (RJ 292) is applied wrongly
research_questions: Does the AFAS fixed asset module support rules per asset class for automatic proposals?
How many register corrections did the auditor raise last year?
Is fleet usage data (hours, kilometres) available to support life estimates?
